content.value_statement: Teams often add motion without a clear user benefit, which can make interfaces feel slow or distracting. This skill audits UI seams, applies a strict decision gate, and produces a short ranked list of precise motion recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Reviews a codebase or interface for UI states that may benefit from motion.
Ranks up to seven opportunities by user value and expected frequency.
Tests every candidate against frequency, purpose, speed, and functional impact.
Provides exact durations, easing, properties, and motion direction for accepted ideas.
Documents rejected candidates so unnecessary animation is not added.
Recommends reduced-motion and input-device considerations for applicable interactions.
limitations: Does not implement, modify, or test animation code.
Cannot judge visual feel or brand personality fully from source code alone.
Requires accessible code or UI context to identify evidence-based opportunities.
Does not replace user research or performance testing on real devices.

use_cases.title: Audit a product interface
use_cases.description: Find a small set of useful motion improvements before a design polish release.

use_cases.title: Prioritize frontend motion work
use_cases.description: Give engineers file-level evidence and precise motion recipes for the highest-value interactions.

use_cases.title: Review an accessible experience
use_cases.description: Reject decorative or frequent animations that could slow down task-focused users.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: inspect one screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the settings screen for animation opportunities. Report only ideas that pass the full gate and include rejected candidates.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: audit a feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the checkout flow for restrained animation opportunities. Prioritize feedback, spatial consistency, and error-state clarity. Do not modify code.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: use existing tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this codebase for animation opportunities. First identify the motion library and shared duration and easing tokens. Then report no more than seven evidence-based recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: protect task speed
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the dashboard for animation opportunities, but reject keyboard-driven, high-frequency, and data-reading interactions. Include reduced-motion guidance for every accepted recommendation.

output_examples.input: Review toast notifications in an application.
output: Opportunity: Toast notifications appear instantly when saved.
Purpose: Preventing a jarring change at an occasional frequency.
Suggested motion: Enter from the same edge with opacity and vertical translation over 250 milliseconds.
Rejected: Command menu opening is keyboard-driven and high-frequency.

output_examples.input: Review a settings page with accordions and toggle controls.
output: Opportunity: An occasional accordion opens without a visual bridge.
Suggested motion: Transition height and opacity within the existing duration tokens.
Rejected: Frequent toggle changes need only near-imperceptible feedback.

best_practices: Provide the relevant files, routes, or screenshots before requesting an audit.
Use existing motion tokens and component conventions when evaluating recommendations.
Treat rejected candidates as useful decisions, not missing output.
anti_patterns: Do not request animation for every interaction or decorative effect.
Do not apply motion to keyboard-driven or high-frequency task flows.
Do not use recommendations without validating reduced-motion behavior and performance.

faq.question: Does this skill change my code?
faq.answer: No. It is read-only and produces recommendations only.

faq.question: How many recommendations will it provide?
faq.answer: It caps a whole-app audit at five to seven suggestions, often fewer.

faq.question: Can it review existing animations?
faq.answer: No. It finds missing opportunities. Use a dedicated animation review skill for existing motion.

faq.question: Does it recommend motion for every interaction?
faq.answer: No. Its gate is designed to reject most candidates that lack a clear user benefit.

faq.question: Does it consider accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. Accepted recommendations include reduced-motion guidance when it applies.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide source files, a route, screenshots, or a description of the interface and user tasks.
